title: Kafka ingestion readout: 40 min to ~9 min, month-end still open
subtitle: May 24, 2023 working session. Numbers, remaining file-drop path, RailClear dual-write. Not a launch party.
author: Aman Kumar
audience: Helen Cho (ops), Marcus Bell (TAM), Priya Nair (EM), Rahul Deshmukh (PM). Copy Chris Patel.
owners: Aman Kumar (notes and ingest-api), Priya Nair (decision log), Helen Cho (ops acceptance)
summary: Readout after Kafka ingestion landed in prod on May 8. Inbound settlement files that used to sit 38-44 minutes from SFTP land to match-engine ack now run 7.4 min on a quiet day and 8.8 min at peak (May 15-23 measured). Helen Cho is not signing off on month-end. April month-end on the old path was 41.2 min; we have not yet had a Kafka month-end. Decision: keep the file-drop path as emergency-only for 90 days (through August 22). Open: RailClear dual-write, who owns the 16:00 ET file they still emit. Next steps assigned. This note is for the people in the room, not a win announcement.

blocks.label: Decisions in the room (Priya confirmed before we hung up)
blocks.text: 1) Kafka path is the default for clh.settlement.inbound as of May 8. We are not rolling back to SFTP-as-primary. 2) File-drop (sftp://files.prod.clearhaven.internal/inbound/settlement/) stays as an emergency path for 90 days, through August 22, 2023, then we disable the consumer unless a Sev-2 forces an extension Priya signs. 3) Helen does not accept month-end as done. First Kafka month-end is May 31 / June 1. Ops review June 2. 4) RailClear dual-write stays open; Marcus takes it to their TAM by May 31. 5) No press, no customer email. Internal Slack #clh-ingest only.
What actually landed

Cutover was Monday May 8, 09:40 ET, not the Thursday May 4 we had on the calendar. May 4 we aborted at 08:12 because MSK connect-clh-prod had a connector in FAILED (S3 sink, unrelated, Diego restarted it, we still slipped). May 8 was a quiet cash day. We flipped ingest-api from the file poller (poll every 30s on the SFTP drop) to the Kafka consumer group ingest-api-prod-cg on topic clh.settlement.inbound, 24 partitions, compression lz4. Producers are the new landing service land-api:2.3.1, which still accepts the same FIX-ish file from the counterparty gateways and publishes one message per leg. Design is CLH-TDD-2023-008. This meeting is the readout, not a redesign.

What did not land: we did not turn off the SFTP listener. land-api still writes a copy to /inbound/settlement/archive/ for 14 days. The old poller is stopped (systemctl stop ingest-file-poller on the four ingest hosts) but the unit file is there. Helen asked, twice, whether anyone can start it without her. Answer: yes, on-call can. That is the emergency path. We will put a Slack mention to #clh-ops when it starts. We did not have that mention on May 8. We do now, as of this morning, CH-ING-1201.

Match-engine did not change. Same EC2 workers, same AMI, same consumer group match-engine-prod on a downstream topic clh.settlement.matched. The latency cut is inbound land-to-match-ack, not matching itself. Kavya wanted that said out loud because people in Slack were writing 'matching is 9 minutes now.' Matching was never 40 minutes. The file sat on SFTP.
Numbers, May 15 through May 23

Definition we used in the room, same as CLH-MEM-2023-004: land-to-match-ack is timestamp of land-api produce (Kafka record timestamp) to timestamp of match-engine's first ack write on break.leg_status for that leg_id. Quiet day means < 1.2M legs inbound. Peak means 1.8-2.4M, which is what we saw May 17 (options expire Friday) and May 19 (a RailClear catch-up). I pulled this from Chris's table ingest.latency_daily, not from Datadog, because Datadog's p99 was still on the old SFTP dashboard for three days after the cut and I do not trust it yet. Sneha flagged that in CH-ING-1184. Fix is in flight, not done.

blocks.caption: Land-to-match-ack, minutes. Pre-cut baseline is April 10-28 SFTP path, 14 business days. Post-cut is May 15-23, 7 business days. We skipped May 8-12 as soak.

blocks.text: Helen looked at the 14.7 max and asked if that was a stall. It was. May 19 15:52 ET, consumer group ingest-api-prod-cg paused 96 seconds during a deploy of land-api:2.3.2 (a log-line fix). Lag hit 180k messages, drained in 6.4 minutes. Match-ack p99 for that hour is the 12.4. I would rather show that than hide it. The old SFTP path hid stalls inside the 40 minute poll+parse. We will see more of these because they are now visible. That is a monitoring problem, not a reason to go back.

Quiet day 7.4 min is real. I ran the query twice in the meeting. Chris's job agreed within 0.2 min. The 7.4 is p50, not a best-case anecdote. p99 quiet is 8.9. If someone quotes 'we hit 7 minutes' to leadership, they should quote p50 and p99 together or not quote at all. Rahul, please.

Where the 7.4 goes. land-api produce is 0.4-1.1s after the gateway POST. Kafka end-to-end on clh-msk-prod is 12-40s p95 (the 40s is when we hit a partition that has a slow ingest-api pod; we have 8 pods and 24 partitions, assignor range, which is a known mess). ingest-api parse+write to Postgres clh-recon-prod is 1.8-3.2 min at peak because we still insert break.raw_leg row-by-row. match-engine consume+ack is 2.1-4.6 min depending on the local redis on the EC2 box. I am not opening a compute memo in this meeting. Priya already has that on a later calendar.
Helen: month-end is not done

Helen came with the April 28 sheet. Ops exception queue depth at 18:00 ET on April 28 was 2,841. Age of oldest row 54 min. She will not compare that to May 16 (depth 312, age 11 min) and call the project done. April 28 is month-end. May 16 is a Tuesday. She is right.

What she needs by June 2, after the May close: exception queue depth at 18:00 ET, age of oldest EXC-HOLD, count of legs that landed after 16:15 ET (RailClear cutoff), and a list of any file-drop emergency starts. If depth is over 1,200 or anything landed after 16:15 that should have made the RailClear file, she will ask to keep file-drop as a parallel path, not emergency-only. Priya agreed that is a fair gate. We did not agree to keep SFTP as primary. We agreed Helen can reopen the 90-day clock if May close is ugly.

Month-end specifics we know will bite. ingest-api still does a serial flush of break.raw_leg around 15:50-16:10 because of a lock on break.leg_status that match-engine holds during the settlement window. On SFTP that flush was invisible inside the 40 minutes. On Kafka you will watch lag climb. Kavya knows. She is not in the room. I told Helen we will have Diego on pager 15:00-17:00 May 31 and June 1, and I will be in the channel. That is the plan, not a promise the lock is gone. The lock is a different ticket (CH-MAT-882, not this project).

Helen also asked about the 11.4 minute clock incident from March (CLH-INC-2023-041 was TLS; the clock one is later, she may be mixing them). Point stands: if ingest is fast and match-engine hosts are skewed, she gets a thin file and a fat exception queue. Kafka does not fix AMI drift. I said that. She said she knows. She still wants the June 2 review.
File-drop emergency path, 90 days

Rejected in the room: 'just leave SFTP running in parallel forever.' Marcus floated it as a customer comfort thing. Priya killed it. Parallel ingest is how you double-post legs. We already have an idempotency key on leg_id+batch_id, but the May 9 shadow showed 0.07% of legs where the SFTP copy and the Kafka copy got different batch_id values because land-api stamps batch_id at produce time and the archive writer used the filename. If both consumers run, those 0.07% look like two legs. Chris has the rows. We will not run both consumers.

Emergency path means: on-call starts ingest-file-poller, land-api Kafka producer is paused (a flag in app_config, key ingest.kafka_produce=false), and we drain SFTP. Only Priya or Helen can call that. Runbook stub is in CH-ING-1201. I will write the actual commands into CLH-RB-2023-012 as a sibling section this week. 90 days is August 22. On August 22 we remove the systemd unit, not just stop it. Rahul wanted 180 days. He did not get it. 90 is already a courtesy for Helen's month-end and for RailClear's dual-write unknown.

blocks.label: Do not start the poller as a test
blocks.text: Sneha's comment in CH-ING-1184: staging still has both consumers on, which is why staging double-counted 1,104 legs on May 11. Staging is not a model for prod. Prod poller stays stopped. If QA needs a file-drop drill, they get a dated window and Kafka produce off. Aman will schedule that with Sneha for the week of June 12, not before May close.

items: Page: ingest-api-prod Sev-2, or Helen in #clh-ops saying the Kafka path is stuck and settlement is at risk.
On-call confirms consumer lag on ingest-api-prod-cg is not draining (CLH-RB-2023-012) and Priya or Helen says go.
Set ingest.kafka_produce=false in app_config, bounce land-api. Confirm produce rate 0 on the Datadog board (the one Chris trusts, ingest-kafka-produce, not the old SFTP board).
systemctl start ingest-file-poller on ingest-01a through 04b. Watch /inbound/settlement/ for new files.
Post in #clh-ops and #clh-ingest: emergency path ON, ticket id, who approved.
When Kafka is healthy: stop poller first, then ingest.kafka_produce=true. Never the other way around.

blocks.text: Open: RailClear dual-write

RailClear still drops a file on SFTP every 16:00 ET (their clock, they mean 16:00 ET) AND they started publishing to a Kafka topic they own, railclear.outbound.legs, which we mirror onto clh.settlement.inbound via a MirrorMaker 2 connector mm2-railclear that Diego stood up April 27. We are consuming the mirrored topic. We are also, some days, getting the file. land-api dedupes on their trade_ref if it sees both. May 15-23: 18.4% of RailClear legs arrived twice, file and Kafka, and the file was 6.2-11.8 min later. Dedup held. The emergency poller, if started, would see those files as new work unless we keep the archive writer running. This is messy.

Marcus's position: RailClear's TAM told him they will stop the file 'in Q3.' That is not a date. We need a date, a last-file flag, and a week of Kafka-only from them before August 22. If they cannot, we either extend file-drop for RailClear only (ugly, special case in the poller) or we tell them the file is ignored after August 22 and they can page us. Helen does not want a special case. I do not want a special case. Marcus will ask for a dated cut. Due May 31, before month-end noise eats the thread.

Rejected: stand up a second consumer group just for RailClear files. That is the parallel path under another name. Also rejected: have land-api drop RailClear Kafka messages on the floor if a file for the same trade_ref exists in archive/. That inverts the default we just set. Kafka is the default. The file is the spare tire. Spare tires do not override the wheel because they showed up later.

Technical leftover: mm2-railclear uses replication factor 2 on the mirror and we have seen 2.4s extra latency vs our own land-api produces. Fine. The connector sits in connect-clh-prod. If it dies, RailClear Kafka legs stop and the file is the only path, which is exactly the emergency we kept. Diego is not in the room; Aman will write him a note to put mm2-railclear on the same pager as ingest-api. It is not there today. That is a gap. I noticed it preparing this meeting, not during the cut. My miss.
What still hurts at ~9 min

row-by-row insert into break.raw_leg. Chris timed 1.8-3.2 min of the quiet-day 7.4. COPY or batched insert is a follow-up (CH-ING-1210, Kavya+Aman, not this quarter unless May close forces it). The table is unpartitioned. We know. Partitioning design is a different doc.

Consumer assignor range on 8 pods / 24 partitions. One pod had 6 partitions on May 17, one had 1. The pod with 6 is where the 14.7 max grew. Sticky assignor is CH-ING-1194, Aman, due June 9. Do not wait for a rebalance incident to do this. Staging already showed a 38s stall on restart.

Datadog. The SFTP dashboard is still the default link in the on-call doc. Three people paged off file-age, which is now a stale metric (archive writer still touches files, so file-age looks healthy even if Kafka is dead). Diego's absence is why this did not get fixed this week. Aman will change the on-call doc today to point at ingest-kafka-lag. Ticket CH-OPS-1904, was opened April 20, still open. I will nag.

Idempotency 0.07% batch_id mismatch. Fixed in land-api:2.3.2, shipped May 19, which is the deploy that paused the consumer 96 seconds. We will watch for a week. If it reappears, Chris's shadow job flags it in the morning mail. Helen wants that mail to go to #clh-ops, not just #clh-ingest. Agreed.
Rejected during the meeting

blocks.text: Engineer appendix: queries we ran in the room
So the next readout is not a hunt through my laptop. All times converted to ET in the view. Postgres clh-recon-prod, role ingest_ro.

blocks.caption: Land-to-match-ack daily, the numbers in the table. Chris owns the view; do not edit it in prod.
blocks.text:
-- ingest.latency_daily is maintained by job latency_daily_refresh (Airflow, 06:15 ET)
SELECT day, slice, p50_min, p95_min, p99_min, max_min, legs
FROM ingest.latency_daily
WHERE day BETWEEN DATE '2023-05-15' AND DATE '2023-05-23'
ORDER BY day, slice;

-- live lag, consumer group ingest-api-prod-cg (run against the lag exporter, not Kafka CLI in the meeting)
-- Datadog: avg:kafka.consumer.lag{consumergroup:ingest-api-prod-cg,env:prod}
-- CLI if Datadog is lying:
-- kubectl -n clh-connect exec kafka-tools-0 -- \
--   kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server b-1.clh-msk-prod.c7.kafka.us-east-1.amazonaws.com:9092 \
--   --group ingest-api-prod-cg --describe

-- exception queue at 18:00 ET, Helen's number
SELECT COUNT(*) AS depth,
       EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (NOW() - MIN(opened_at))) / 60.0 AS oldest_min
FROM break.exception_queue
WHERE status IN ('OPEN','EXC-HOLD')
  AND opened_at < TIMESTAMPTZ '2023-05-23 18:00:00-04';

May 19 stall, for the record. land-api:2.3.2 rolled at 15:51:08 ET. Consumer paused 15:51:12-15:52:48. Max lag 180,412. Drain complete 15:59:04. Deploy flag --wait was not used. I used it on the next deploy. If you ship ingest during 15:30-16:30 you will see this again. Freeze next week includes that window every day, not just May 31.
What this meeting was not

It was not a launch. Latency moved from ~40 min to ~9 min on ordinary days because we stopped polling a directory every 30 seconds and parsing 400 MB files in one process. That is the whole trick. Month-end, RailClear's file, the range assignor, the Postgres inserts, and the EC2 match-engine hosts are still there. Helen will tell us on June 2 whether ops can live with that. Until then, quote the table, keep the spare tire, and do not start the poller to see if it still works.
